step1_figure.circuit_type: Two-stage CMOS op-amp with indirect feedback compensation
step1_figure.description: Figure 24.21 shows a two-stage operational amplifier implementing indirect feedback compensation without additional power dissipation. The compensation capacitor Cc (240 fF) feeds current back to the low-impedance node between cascode load devices M4T and M4B to eliminate the right-half-plane (RHP) zero and enhance bandwidth.

equation.explanation: Product of the first-stage differential gain (gm1*R1) and the second-stage common-source gain (gm2*R2).
equation.assumptions: Low frequency where reactive impedances are negligible; small-signal conditions.

sky130_expected.calculation: With I_tail = 20 uA (I_D1 = 10 uA), (W/L)1 = 50/2 = 25, mu_n*Cox = 270 uA/V^2: gm1 = sqrt(2 * 270e-6 * 25 * 10e-6) = 367 uS. First-stage output resistance R1 ≈ ro1 || (gm4b * ro4b * ro4t) ≈ ro1 ≈ 1/(0.1 * 10 uA) = 1 MOhm. A1 ≈ 367. For second stage (PMOS M7), I_D7 ≈ 10 uA, (W/L)7 = 100/2 = 50, mu_p*Cox = 50 uA/V^2: gm2 = sqrt(2 * 50e-6 * 50 * 10e-6) = 224 uS. R2 ≈ ro7 || (gm8t * ro8t * ro8b) ≈ ro7 ≈ 1 MOhm. A2 ≈ 224. A_OL_DC = 367 * 224 ≈ 82,200 ≈ 98 dB. Accounting for subthreshold effects and lower channel length output resistances in sky130, gain typically lands around 65-80 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Finite transistor output conductance and loading in SKY130 reduce ideal intrinsic gain.

unity_gain_frequency.description: Frequency where the open-loop gain drops to 0 dB (unity)

equation.explanation: Unity-gain frequency set by the input stage transconductance gm1 and the indirect compensation capacitance Cc.

sky130_expected.calculation: gm1 ≈ 367 uS, Cc = 240 fF. f_un = 367e-6 / (2 * pi * 240e-15) ≈ 243 MHz (in 1.8V Sky130 technology).
sky130_expected.reasoning: High transconductance of the 50/2 NMOS pair at 10 uA branch current combined with a small 240 fF capacitor yields bandwidth near 200 MHz.

phase_margin.description: Phase angle difference from -180 degrees at the unity-gain frequency

equation.explanation: Measure of closed-loop stability and damping. Indirect compensation introduces a LHP zero that boosts PM.

sky130_expected.calculation: The LHP zero created by indirect compensation provides lead phase boost near unity gain. For Cc = 240 fF driving CL = 100 fF, PM is designed to exceed 70 degrees.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Indirect compensation eliminates the RHP zero and shifts the second pole higher, giving high phase margin.

gain_margin.description: Difference between 0 dB and the open-loop gain when the phase shift reaches -180 degrees

equation.explanation: Gain reduction needed to reach instability at the frequency where phase is -180 degrees.

sky130_expected.calculation: With high second-pole frequency (f2 > 500 MHz) and LHP zero, the phase crossover occurs well above 500 MHz where gain is depressed by >15 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Baker reports ~25 dB GM for compensated op-amp.

lhp_zero_frequency.description: Location of the left-half-plane zero introduced by indirect feedback

equation.explanation: Zero frequency determined by the transconductance of the common-gate connection (M4B) and compensation capacitor Cc.
equation.assumptions: Current feedback via common-gate action of M4B.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Sized to approximately match or exceed the unity gain frequency for lead compensation.

second_pole_frequency.description: Frequency of the non-dominant high-frequency pole

equation.explanation: Second pole pushed to higher frequency by the indirect feedback mechanism compared to standard Miller.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Indirect compensation places the non-dominant pole significantly higher than Miller compensation.

slew_rate_positive.description: Maximum rate of output voltage increase during a large positive input step

equation.explanation: Positive slewing rate is limited by the diff-amp tail bias current Iss charging the compensation capacitor Cc.
equation.assumptions: Diff-pair completely steers current Iss into Cc.

sky130_expected.calculation: Iss = 20 uA, Cc = 240 fF. SR+ = 20 uA / 240 fF = 83.3 V/us (or 83.3 mV/ns).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Since Cc is reduced from 2.4 pF to 240 fF in indirect compensation, SR+ improves tenfold.

slew_rate_negative.description: Maximum rate of output voltage decrease during a large negative input step

equation.explanation: Negative slewing rate is limited by current sink M8 discharging the combined output capacitance (CL + Cc).
equation.assumptions: M7 is turned off; M8 sinks constant bias current.

sky130_expected.calculation: I_M8 = 10 uA, CL = 100 fF, Cc = 240 fF (total = 340 fF). SR- = 10 uA / 340 fF ≈ 29.4 V/us (with CL = 1 pF, SR- = 10 uA / 1.24 pF ≈ 8 V/us).
sky130_expected.reasoning: M8 constant current discharge defines high-to-low slewing slope.

cmrr.description: Common-Mode Rejection Ratio at low frequency

equation.explanation: Ratio of differential-mode gain to common-mode gain, primarily determined by the input diff-pair.

sky130_expected.calculation: Cascode tail current source (M6T, M6B) provides output resistance > 10 MOhm. Ad ≈ 367, Ac ≈ 1/(2*gm4b*R_tail) ≈ 0.001. CMRR ≈ 20*log10(367 / 0.001) ≈ 60-75 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Cascode tail current source maintains high CMRR.

psrr_positive.description: Power Supply Rejection Ratio from VDD to output

equation.explanation: Rejection of noise injected on the VDD supply rail relative to differential gain.

sky130_expected.calculation: At DC, circuit symmetry attenuates VDD supply noise to vout/v+ ≈ 1, so PSRR+ ≈ A_OL_DC ≈ 65-75 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: DC PSRR+ follows open loop gain.

psrr_negative.description: Power Supply Rejection Ratio from GND to output

equation.explanation: Rejection of noise injected on the ground rail relative to differential gain.

sky130_expected.calculation: Cascode tail current sources isolate the amplifier from ground bounce, yielding PSRR- ≈ 65-80 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Cascode NMOS current sources offer very high impedance to ground.

power_dissipation.description: Total static DC power consumption of the op-amp and bias circuit

equation.explanation: Product of supply voltage and total current drawn from VDD (diff-amp + second stage + bias circuit).

sky130_expected.calculation: Diff-amp current = 20 uA, output stage current = 10 uA, bias circuit current ≈ 35 uA. Total current ≈ 65 uA. At VDD = 1.8 V: P = 1.8 V * 65 uA ≈ 117 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Low bias current operation for analog processing in 1.8V domain.

step3_testbench.description: ngspice testbench for the indirectly compensated op-amp (Fig 24.21). Performs DC operating point (power), open-loop AC analysis (gain, bandwidth, PM, GM, CMRR, PSRR using Baker RC replica feedback), and large-signal transient step response (SR+, SR-, settling).
